knowledge:
- key_parameters: weights=A matrix of weights corresponding to measurements, where a weight of 0 indicates missing data ;; design=A design matrix for linear model fitting ;; trend_formula=A formula used in calibration to model squared residuals (e.g., using well_knotted_spline) ;; p=The number of components of variation to discover ;; coef=The coefficient to test in differential analysis ;; contrasts=Contrasts matrix specifying the subspace of coefficients to test
- alternatives: limma::voom/vooma=Similar to weitrix_calibrate_all, but weitrix allows more complex models and works on already log-transformed data ;; limma::eBayes(trend=TRUE)=Similar to weitrix_calibrate_trend, but weitrix allows other predictors beyond the row average ;; limma (via weitrix_elist)=Traditional differential expression analysis, though limma's use of weights is approximate for contrasts or F-tests
- when_to_use: When working with high-throughput transcriptomics data where observations have varying precision (e.g., average poly(A) tail lengths weighted by read counts, alternative polyadenylation shift scores, or exon junction proportions) and when there is a need to perform PCA-like dimension reduction on matrices with uneven weights or missing values
- pitfalls: Using uncalibrated weights can lead to suboptimal testing results; always calibrate weights first using weitrix_calibrate_all or weitrix_calibrate_trend and check with weitrix_calplot ;; Using the $col matrix of discovered components as a design matrix for differential analysis with weitrix_confects or limma may produce liberal results because design matrix uncertainty is ignored ;; Multi-threaded BLAS libraries (like OpenBLAS) can slow down parallel processing; use RhpcBLASctl::blas_set_num_threads(1) before starting workers ;; Fork-based worker processes can mess up X11-based plotting; start workers before opening plots

workflows.name: weighted_continuous_matrix_analysis
workflows.intent: Analyze continuous measurements with associated precision weights (e.g., average tail lengths weighted by read counts) to calibrate weights, find components of variation, and test for differential effects.
workflows.stages: 1. Construct weitrix using as_weitrix ;; 2. Annotate row and column metadata ;; 3. Fit initial components with weitrix_components ;; 4. Calibrate weights using weitrix_calibrate_all with well_knotted_spline ;; 5. Diagnostic plotting with weitrix_calplot ;; 6. Test for top confident effects using weitrix_confects or limma (via weitrix_elist) ;; 7. Discover components of variation using weitrix_components_seq and plot with components_seq_screeplot
workflows.code:
wei <- as_weitrix( tail[good,,drop=FALSE], weights=tail_count[good,,drop=FALSE])
rowData(wei)$gene <- AnnotationDbi::select( org.Sc.sgd.db, keys=rownames(wei), columns=c("GENENAME"))$GENENAME
rowData(wei)$total_reads <- rowSums(weitrix_weights(wei))
colData(wei) <- cbind(colData(wei), samples)
design <- model.matrix(~ strain + time, data=colData(wei))
fit <- weitrix_components(wei, design=design)
cal <- weitrix_calibrate_all( wei, design = fit, trend_formula = ~well_knotted_spline(mu,3)+well_knotted_spline(log(weight),3))
weitrix_calplot(unwei, fit, covar=mu, guides=FALSE)
weitrix_confects(cal, design, coef="strainDeltaSet1", fdr=0.05)
weitrix_confects(cal, design, coef="strainDeltaSet1", effect="cohen_f", fdr=0.05)
fit_cal_design <- cal %>% weitrix_elist() %>% lmFit(design)
ebayes_fit <- eBayes(fit_cal_design)
topTable(ebayes_fit, "strainDeltaSet1", n=10)
multiple_contrasts <- limma::makeContrasts( timet15m-timet0m, timet30m-timet15m, timet45m-timet30m, timet60m-timet45m, timet75m-timet60m, timet90m-timet75m, timet105m-timet90m, timet120m-timet105m, levels=design)
weitrix_confects(cal, design, contrasts=multiple_contrasts, fdr=0.05)
confects <- weitrix_sd_confects(cal, ~1)
comp_seq <- weitrix_components_seq(cal, p=6)
components_seq_screeplot(comp_seq)
comp <- comp_seq[[3]]
matrix_long(comp$col[,-1], row_info=samples, varnames=c("sample","component"))
result_C1 <- weitrix_confects(cal, comp$col, coef="C1")

workflows.name: alternative_polyadenylation_shift_analysis
workflows.intent: Analyze alternative polyadenylation (APA) site-level counts by calculating shift scores, calibrating weights, and identifying components of variation.
input: peaks.csv.gz (data frame grouping sites into genes)
workflows.stages: 1. Construct shift weitrix using counts_shift ;; 2. Find components of variation using weitrix_components_seq ;; 3. Calibrate weights using weitrix_calibrate_all (or weitrix_calibrate_trend for large datasets) with per_read_var and well_knotted_spline ;; 4. Diagnostic plotting with weitrix_calplot ;; 5. Test for confident loadings using weitrix_confects ;; 6. Find highly variable genes using weitrix_sd_confects
workflows.code:
wei <- counts_shift(counts, groups)
colData(wei) <- cbind(colData(wei), samples)
rowData(wei)$symbol <- genes$symbol[match(rownames(wei), rownames(genes))]
comp_seq <- weitrix_components_seq(wei, p=6, design=~0)
components_seq_screeplot(comp_seq)
comp <- comp_seq[[4]]
cal <- weitrix_calibrate_all( wei, design = comp, trend_formula = ~log(per_read_var)+well_knotted_spline(log2(weight),3))
weitrix_calplot(wei, comp, covar=mu)
weitrix_confects(cal, comp$col, "C1", fdr=0.05)
weitrix_sd_confects(cal, step=0.01)
cal_trend <- weitrix_calibrate_trend( wei, design = comp, trend_formula = ~log(per_read_var)+well_knotted_spline(log(total_reads),3))

workflows.name: rna_seq_expression_precision_weights
workflows.intent: Assign precision weights to RNA-Seq log CPM values, calibrate them, and perform exploratory analysis to find genes with excess variation or components of variation.
workflows.stages: 1. Filter and normalize counts using edgeR (filterByExpr, calcNormFactors, cpm) ;; 2. Convert log2 CPM to weitrix using as_weitrix ;; 3. Fit initial linear model using weitrix_components ;; 4. Calibrate weights using weitrix_calibrate_all with well_knotted_spline on predicted expression levels (mu) ;; 5. Find genes with excess variation using weitrix_sd_confects ;; 6. Find components of variation using weitrix_components_seq and compare to randomized data using weitrix_randomize ;; 7. Perform differential testing using weitrix_confects or limma (via weitrix_elist)
workflows.code:
airway_lcpm <- cpm(airway_dgelist, log=TRUE, prior.count=1)
airway_weitrix <- as_weitrix(airway_lcpm)
colData(airway_weitrix) <- colData(airway)
rowData(airway_weitrix) <- mcols(genes(EnsDb.Hsapiens.v86))[rownames(airway_weitrix),c("gene_name","gene_biotype")]
fit <- weitrix_components(airway_weitrix, design=design)
airway_cal <- weitrix_calibrate_all( airway_weitrix, design = fit, trend_formula = ~well_knotted_spline(mu,5))
weitrix_calplot(airway_cal, fit, covar=mu)
confects <- weitrix_sd_confects(airway_cal)
confects2 <- weitrix_sd_confects(airway_cal, assume_normal=FALSE)
comp_seq <- weitrix_components_seq(airway_cal, p=6, n_restarts=1)
rand_weitrix <- weitrix_randomize(airway_cal)
rand_comp <- weitrix_components(rand_weitrix, p=1, n_restarts=1)
components_seq_screeplot(comp_seq, rand_comp)
comp <- comp_seq[[4]]
weitrix_confects(airway_cal, comp$col, "C1")
airway_elist <- weitrix_elist(airway_cal)
fit <- lmFit(airway_elist, comp$col) %>% eBayes()
topTable(fit, "C1")
